answer.summary: Aparna’s heuristic is to look for at least two of three inflection points—technology, user behavior, and business model—and not mistake a better interface alone for a reason customers will switch. While solving the idea, stay open to changing direction before scaling. [S1, S2, S3]

sections.heading: Look for at least two inflection points
sections.content: Aparna says to look for at least two of three factors. One is a step-function change in technology: she cites deep learning for Google Lens, speech recognition for conversational search, and phones enabling a usable mobile finance app for Robinhood; she says LLMs and reasoning models are current examples of a tech inflection. The framework also points to a shift in user behavior and a new business model or monetization approach that creates an advantage. Robinhood’s zero-fee model is an example. Her caution: a more intuitive interface by itself is not enough to expect customers to switch. [S1, S2]

sections.heading: Solve before you scale
sections.content: Treat the early stage as problem-solving, not scaling: be willing to make wide changes as you learn. Aparna’s Google Lens example moved from a plant-detection idea to foreign-language translation by day 15. That illustrates why she advises teams not to rush to scale before they have solved the problem. [S3]
